newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mixed on USDA export data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mixed on USDA export data.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mixed on Thursday with old crop down on lackluster USDA weekly export sales figures while new crop was boosted by strong 1997-98 sales data, pit sources said.
Soyoil was mostly lower with May posting gains in thin volume as shorts got out ahead of Tuesday's expiry.

USDA said U.S. net export sales of soymeal for the week ended May 8 totaled 48,000 tonnes, versus expectations for 40,000 to 60,000 tonnes. Net export sales of soyoil totaled 200 tonnes, below expectations for 5,000 to 8,000 tonnes.
New crop soymeal sales were at 72,800 tonnes.

"Crush may be more important for a while now than the export numbers," said Dale Durchholz, analyst with Agrivisor Services. "Over the last four weeks, crush margins have jumped to levels where processors can make some money."
July crush margins closed up 1.41 cent a bushel at 35.67.
Trade estimates for Thursday's National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush figure ranged from 23.60 million to 25.10 million bushels. Last week's figure was 24.5 million.
Soymeal ended $2.20 per ton lower to $1.30 higher with July off $2.20 at $286.70. Soyoil was 0.12 cent per lb higher to 0.06 lower with July unchanged at 23.88.

Talk China bought one cargo of U.S. soymeal was deemed mildly supportive for August and September futures. Hong Kong traders said a panamax cargo of low protein U.S. soymeal was sold for August/September delivery.

China was also rumored to be buying South American soyoil. Commercial buying in that pit lent credence to the rumor, floor sources said. Continental Grain bought 700 lots July soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 400 July and Produce Grain and Term Commodities each bought 200 July.

Weather also lent some support to new crop. Forecasts called for temperatures to fall into the upper 20s F on Friday in parts of South Dakota, Minnesota and nothern Iowa. That scenario could slow germination.
But some sources said it was too early to worry about weather problems.
"We don't have enough beans out of the ground to have a signficant impact," one trader said.

Soymeal traders continued to eye the liquidation of the May contract. Trade sources said calls were placed this week reminding traders to liquidate the May ahead of expiry on Tuesday. CBOT put May open interest as of Thursday morning at 4,293 lots, down 1,135 from the previous day.

Smith Barney spread 500 lots July/May soymeal at $12.50, premium May, and another 500 lots May/July at $13.00, traders said. Those moves should shave 1,000 lots off of the open interest, traders said.

On the day, SAK Futures sold 1,000 lots July soymeal. Pit sources said the sale sent July futures down half the daily limit in late dealings. R.J. O'Brien sold 400 July and Continental Grain sold 500 July soymeal.
In soyoil, Merrill Lynch sold 500 July and 200 December while Griffin trading sold 200 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 22,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 28,397. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, against Wednesday's 30,667.
